Publishing services

From first draft to finished shelf. Here's how Arikana works with writers to get a book ready for readers.

Developmental & structural editing

We work through your manuscript at the level of story: pacing, character arcs, plot holes, proofreading, and structure. This is the editing pass that happens before a single comma is polished — it's about making sure the book works.

Cover design

A cover that tells a reader exactly what shelf your book belongs on. Our designers build concepts around your genre and market, then refine typography, imagery, and finish until the cover is ready to print or publish online.

Distribution

We get finished books into bookstores, online retailers, and direct to readers across the region and beyond — handling print logistics, e‑book formats, and the retail relationships that keep your book in stock. With our Bookstore partners and global reach, we get your books where it matters: to the readers.

Reach us via our Contacts for more.

The Authors

The people behind the books. Each author's page links straight through to their work.

W.B. Njeru

Author of Son of Akanga & Guerrilla Queen

Wilfred Bundi Njeru is a Kenyan Producer, author and creative based in Nairobi, Kenya. He is the author of the 2023 release, Son Of Akanga - the first title off the ARIKANA book series, circling African Lore and fantasy. The title was selected by the American Embassy as part of their global literature collection, and is now available both in the Library of Congress catalogue and in select libraries across America.

Get Son of Akanga Get Guerrilla Queen

Torben Vestergaard Frandsen & Dolphine Maleshe

Authors of The Anti‑corruption Mandate

Drawing on years of governance and institutional work, Torben Vestergaard Frandsen and Dolphine Maleshe co‑wrote The Anti‑corruption Mandate as a practical guide — 41 concrete steps to help curb corruption in governmental, institutional, and organisational systems.

Get The Anti‑corruption Mandate

Wandera Ogana

Author of Mathematics Contest & Little Hesabu Friends

Wandera Ogana is an esteemed Mathematician and a Retired Professor of Mathematics from the University of Nairobi. He received a PhD in Applied Mathematics from Stanford University, USA, in 1975. His literary publications include Hand of Chance (1970), Days of Glamour (1975), Campus Days(2007), A Family Affair (2011), Little Hesabu Friends (2026), and Mathematics Contest (2026).
